They also explained that the order of eating main and side dishes varies depending on the food. Furthermore, they mentioned that they prefer the tender thigh part when eating chicken. dialogue:
Speaker1: Have you ever heard anything about your personality, like being outgoing or shy?
Speaker2: A lot of people think I'm super shy and reserved before getting to know me, but once we’re close, they usually say I’m loud and outgoing.
Speaker2: I guess I've heard a mix of being shy at first and then lively later on.
Speaker2: I'm curious what you think your personality is, then.
Speaker1: I've heard a lot of similar things too, like before getting close, people say I'm really quiet or deep in thought. But once we get to know each other, it's like, how can this person be like that? I guess I end up being known as a really lively friend with some pretty weird thoughts.
Speaker1: So I think my true personality is closer to the latter. I mean, I don’t think the way others see me is accurate.
Speaker1: Hmm, so what kind of personality do you think you vibe with?
Speaker2: I think if someone with a really outgoing personality approaches me first, it’d help me warm up and get close faster since I’m super shy at first.
Speaker2: I prefer someone lively and, above all, kind and considerate.
Speaker2: So, if there's a part of my personality I'd want to change, what would it be?
Speaker1: I’m also really shy, so I wanna work on that. I’ve had a lot of struggles when talking on the phone or with new people because I get super awkward, and it often leads to those awkward pauses in conversation. It’s stressful feeling that pressure to keep the chat going, so I’d like to be a bit more outgoing.
Speaker1: Have you ever had a tough experience because of your personality?
Speaker2: I'm not very confident, so I can talk well in front of close friends, but with strangers, I can't really express my opinions and just kinda go with the flow.
Speaker2: I often end up just going along with others and not saying what I need to, and then I get home and feel all stressed about it, wishing I could just speak up and say what's wrong.
Speaker2: So, do you have a personality where you think, "I want to be seen this way by others"?
Speaker1: Hmm, I wanna be remembered as a kind person who's considerate and doesn't hurt others.
Speaker1: So I wanna be remembered as someone who helps a lot, has skills, and is thoughtful—basically, someone fun to be around and someone people wanna spend more time with.
Speaker1: Have you ever tried to change that, like doing something about those times you struggled to speak up and ended up suffering alone because of your personality?
Speaker2: I've tried doing more presentations and organizing my thoughts before speaking, but I haven't really put in the effort I should, so I think I need to try harder now.
Speaker2: So, if you don't really wanna be friends with someone like that, I'm curious what that personality is and why.
Speaker1: I find it really hard to be friends with people who don’t keep their promises. I’ve had friends like that who would always be late or just not show up at all, and it happened so often that I ended up wasting my time and feelings every time.
Speaker1: I’ve had a tough time with those experiences, and since those friends often ghosted me too, I really don’t want to be friends with people who cause those kinds of issues anymore. So, I’m not into friends who are late or don’t take commitments seriously.
Speaker1: So, I wrote down the same question. Is there a type of personality you’d want to avoid in friends?
Speaker2: I really can’t stand friends who are not only unreliable but also super self-centered and don’t consider other people's feelings.
Speaker2: If a friend’s all about their own superiority and doesn’t care about how their words or actions hurt others, I definitely don’t want to be friends with that kind of person.
Speaker2: So if you had to pick one thing, what do you think is the most important trait in relationships or social life?
Speaker1: I think it’s definitely gotta be being perceptive. You could say it’s about reading the room well, too.
Speaker1: I think being able to read the emotions of your coworkers, whether they're above or below you, and considering what you can do based on that is super helpful in the workplace and in social life moving forward.
Speaker1: For sure, being able to consider others is way more important in a workplace where people clash than just having the skills and being able to show them off.
Speaker1: Do you like your personality?
Speaker2: I really don’t like my personality, to be honest. I often think I should do better but end up procrastinating, and there are times I feel like I should say something but don’t, so I really want to change it.
Speaker2: So, which personality do you think is better or worse: the one that says everything without filtering, even if it might hurt the other person, or the one that holds back and keeps everything to themselves?
Speaker1: I personally think it's better to have a friend who speaks their mind without filtering if we're close, but if it's a more distant relationship, keeping things to yourself is probably better.
Speaker1: If we're gonna be close for a long time, I’d want my flaws pointed out so I can fix them. That way, I can be a better friend and a cooler person for them. But if we’re not that close, I really don’t wanna hear any judgments or bad talk about me when they don’t even know me well.
Speaker1: What do you think a good personality is like?
Speaker2: I think the best personality is one that’s kind and considerate of others but also knows how to stand up for themselves and can express their opinions well.
Speaker2: I think kindness and quick thinking are super important because they help with relationships, and even if people underestimate you, you can overcome that with your personality.
Speaker1: You said a good personality is kind and quick-witted, so how close do you think you are to that?
Speaker2: Honestly, I’m not really a fan of my personality, so I think I’ve got a long way to go to meet those good character standards I mentioned.
Speaker2: So, I think I need to put in some effort to get closer to that good personality before I can say mine's good.
Speaker2: So, I'll ask you the same question you asked earlier about personality—have you ever thought deeply about your own or others' personalities?
Speaker1: I tend to reflect pretty deeply on my personality. It's because whenever there's friction with others, I always wonder if there's something wrong with me that's making it hard to get along.
Speaker1: Basically, I’ve learned that while blaming others might feel easier for my peace of mind, it doesn’t help my relationships in the long run. So even when there’s no real issue, I think a lot about why I have these thoughts, what I gain from them, and how they might affect my life moving forward, and what kind of personality that comes from.
Speaker1: I often go for walks with my earbuds in to help me focus on my thoughts.
output: The two people discussed personality in this conversation. speaker1 mentioned that they have a quirky and active personality but are shy at first. They specifically expressed feeling difficulties in communication and want to improve this aspect. They also said they hope to be evaluated as a good person by others and do not want to be close to people who do not keep their promises. Additionally, they stated that being perceptive helps them be considerate, which is beneficial for social life. They explained that when conflicts arise with others, they tend to reflect on whether it is their fault, indicating they think seriously about their personality. speaker2 expressed dissatisfaction with their own personality, saying they are indecisive and lack confidence. They mentioned having faced many difficulties because of this and are trying to overcome it, but still feel there are many areas for improvement. They also noted that due to their lack of sociability, they get along well with more outgoing people. They said they are introverted at first but become extroverted after getting close to someone. They believe a good personality is someone who is kind yet assertive about their opinions. Conversely, they stated they do not want to be close to self-centered and inconsiderate people.

dialogue:
Speaker1: So, you’ve probably heard of that personality test called MBTI, right? I’d love to hear your thoughts on it.
Speaker2: I know the MBTI test has been around for a long time. I actually took it for the first time in elementary school and have done it for fun ever since. I always get the same type, and since it’s based on questions related to my personality, I think it’s got some level of reliability.
Speaker2: But I've noticed lately that some people are putting way too much faith in MBTI and often use it to judge others. I've even heard of some companies requiring MBTI results as a must when applying for jobs.
Speaker2: I think these things shouldn't happen. While the MBTI has some reliability as a personality test, it shouldn't be used as an absolute measure to evaluate people, and the more people blindly trust or get too into it, the more these situations will likely occur, which worries me.
Speaker2: Have you ever thought deeply about personality? Like your own or someone else's, just personality in general.
Speaker1: I haven't really thought about my own personality, but I've definitely thought a lot about other people's.
Speaker1: I always think about other people's personalities, like what kind of personality they have that hurts me when I'm stressed or what kind makes me feel good.
Speaker1: Talking like this makes me think it’s not great to judge others' personalities just by my own standards.
Speaker1: So earlier I asked about your thoughts on MBTI, but now I'm curious about personality by blood type.
Speaker2: Blood type personalities have been popular for a long time, and I think the trend has faded a bit now. In the past, I really liked blood type personalities because they made it easy to categorize my own personality into four types and figure out which one I fit into.
Speaker2: So, I liked that I could just know my type and compare it to my own personality, but it's already been shown that blood type and personality aren't really linked, and the number of people who believe in it is dropping, so I guess I don't have a great view on blood type personalities anymore.
Speaker2: It’s fun to look at for kicks, but I don’t wanna be close to anyone who takes blood type personalities too seriously.
Speaker2: I'd like to ask you the same question—what do you think about the MBTI personality test?
Speaker1: I personally really like the MBTI personality test and tend to believe in it. It’s fun to discover aspects of my type that I didn’t even know about, and it’s interesting to compare them.
Speaker1: But I think it's bad to get too caught up in MBTI or those personality tests and judge others or just assume my personality is this way without question.
output: The two people discussed MBTI and personality traits based on blood types in this conversation. speaker1 said they tend to think a lot about other people's personalities rather than their own. They explained that they look for and analyze the causes of changes in their emotional state from the other person. They mentioned that while they have a positive view of MBTI, they only refer to it for fun and do not use it to evaluate others. speaker2 said they have taken the MBTI and believe it has some credibility. However, they expressed concern about some companies incorporating MBTI into their hiring evaluation criteria. They also explained that they had classified personalities based on blood types and enjoyed it, but after realizing it was not scientific and lacked reliability, they now have a negative view of it.
